blocks.text: The chapter presents brief sayings about upbringing, debt, diligence, wealth, and treatment of the poor. Proverbs is designed to teach through compact, context-sensitive generalizations and deliberate juxtapositions, rather than treating each saying as an exceptionless promise. That matters here: the warning that borrowers become dependent on lenders stands beside condemnation of exploiting the poor, and instruction about wise living stands beside a command not to rob or oppress those already vulnerable.

The instruction beginning at Proverbs 22:17 continues through 24:22. This sequence shares unusually close themes and expressions with the Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope. The parallel is debated, but it helps identify these verses as part of an extended body of instruction rather than merely another isolated proverb.
